variables.event: winning something they never expected to win

prompt_text: Write how someone would tell their friend about winning something they never expected to win.
system_text: Write the way someone tells a friend a story out loud — casual spoken language, like you're just hanging out. Output only what they say, no labels or quotation marks.
response:
Okay, so you will not believe what happened to me Saturday. Sit down. Actually, you're already sitting, fine, but still.

So you know how Dana dragged me to that fundraiser thing for the animal shelter? The one at the old fire station? I did not want to go. I was like, I'm tired, I wanna stay in, whatever. But I felt bad, so I went. And they're selling raffle tickets, right, five bucks each, and I'm thinking, okay, it's for the dogs, I'll buy one. Just one. I don't win stuff. Like ever. I have never won anything in my entire life. I once lost a coin flip against myself, I swear.

So I stuff the ticket in my back pocket and I completely forget about it. I'm over by the snack table, talking to this guy about, I don't even know, like cheese dip, and then the lady on the microphone starts calling numbers. And she's doing the little stuff first, gift cards, a candle, whatever. And then she goes, "And our grand prize, a brand new two-person kayak!" And I'm like, cool, somebody's gonna be thrilled.

And then she reads the number, and I'm not even paying attention, and Dana just grabs my arm and goes, "Check your ticket. Check your ticket!" And I'm like, why, and she's yanking my arm like, "Just check it!" So I pull it out, and dude. It was the number. It was my number. I literally just stood there. I couldn't even talk. Somebody had to say, "Hey, is that you?" and I kinda just went, "...I think so?"

And everybody's clapping, and I walk up there like a total zombie, and they hand me this giant paddle, and I'm holding it, and I'm like, thank you, I guess? I don't even know what you say. I think I said "wow" like six times.

And here's the best part. I live on the third floor. In an apartment. With no storage. I don't even have a car that can fit it! Dana had to drive it home on her roof rack, and she kept saying, "You're a kayak guy now," and I'm like, I am not a kayak guy! I've been on a boat twice!

But honestly? It's kind of amazing. It's just sitting in my living room right now, taking up the whole wall, and every time I walk past it I start laughing. So anyway, you're coming with me next weekend. I don't care if it's cold. We're figuring this out.
